# pidginhost_volume_attachment (Resource)

Attaches an existing volume to a server (`/api/cloud/volumes/{id}/attach/`); destroying it detaches the volume without deleting it.

Use it for volumes that are not managed by `pidginhost_volume`, for example the extra volume created with a server (`extra_volume_product`) or volumes created in the control panel. A `pidginhost_volume` already keeps its volume attached to its `server_id`; do not manage the same volume with both.

If the volume is already attached to the requested server, creating the attachment adopts it. If it is attached to another server, creation fails rather than moving it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Attach a volume that Terraform did not create (for example one made in the
# control panel) to a server.
resource "pidginhost_volume_attachment" "archive" {
  volume_id = "123"
  server_id = pidginhost_server.db.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `server_id` (String) ID of the server.
- `volume_id` (String) ID of the volume.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<volume_id>/<server_id>`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an attachment as <volume_id>/<server_id>.
terraform import pidginhost_volume_attachment.archive 123/456
```
